territorial_scope.description: Applies to insurers under Colorado law, to protect Colorado residents' access to insurance.

evidence.quote: ensure that all Colorado residents have fair and equitable access to insurance products

summary.short: Colorado SB 21-169 bars insurers from unfairly discriminating on protected characteristics, including through external consumer data, algorithms and predictive models. It requires the insurance commissioner to adopt rules, after a stakeholder process, under which insurers must test and demonstrate non-discrimination.
summary.long: SB 21-169 adds Colorado Revised Statutes section 10-3-1104.9. It prohibits insurers, for any insurance practice, from unfairly discriminating based on race, color, national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, disability, gender identity or gender expression. It also prohibits using external consumer data and information sources, or algorithms and predictive models that use them, in a way that unfairly discriminates on those grounds, as the commissioner's rules permit. The commissioner must hold a stakeholder process and then adopt rules by insurance type and practice. The rules must require insurers to report the external data sources they use, explain their use, maintain a risk management framework, assess results, and provide an officer attestation. The rules must also allow a reasonable period to remedy discriminatory impacts. Rule-making documents are treated as confidential trade secrets. The commissioner may examine and investigate insurers' use of these tools under section 10-3-1106. The section excludes title insurance and surety bonds, and commercial policies except business owners' and general liability policies with annual premiums of $10,000 or less. It does not require insurers to collect protected characteristics. The act takes effect 90 days after final adjournment, subject to referendum.

relations.note: Adds new section 10-3-1104.9 to the Colorado Revised Statutes. Subsection (7)(b)(III) states the section may not be construed to amend, modify or supersede 10-3-1104(1)(f)(III) or (1)(f)(IV).

notes: Text is the enacted act as provided, not a consolidated version. No enabling act is cited. Subsection (5) is repealed by its own terms effective July 1, 2025 (5)(b); no other instrument is repealed. Subsection (1)(a) prohibits unfair discrimination directly, while (1)(b) reaches certain data use only 'pursuant to rules adopted by the commissioner', and rules may not take effect before January 1, 2023 (3)(a). Section 3 sets the effective date by reference to adjournment and referendum; no calendar date is stated. Subsection (6)(c) excludes commercial insurance policies except business owners' and commercial general liability policies with annual premiums of $10,000 or less.

thresholds.variable_text: annual premiums of business owners' policies or commercial general liability policies
thresholds.value_text: ANNUAL PREMIUMS OF TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS OR LESS
thresholds.measurement: Annual premium of the business owners' or commercial general liability policy issued by the insurer
thresholds.consequence: The section applies to insurers issuing business owners' or commercial general liability policies at or below this annual premium, although it otherwise excludes insurers issuing commercial insurance policies.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only to business owners' policies or commercial general liability policies; the general exclusion for commercial insurance policies in the same subsection still applies to other commercial policies.

evidence.quote: WHICH BUSINESS OWNERS' POLICIES OR COMMERCIAL GENERAL LIABILITY POLICIES HAVE ANNUAL PREMIUMS OF TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS OR LESS
